name: Arch Linux ARM terminal for Surface Pro 11 — v23 (experimental)
body:
# Arch Linux ARM terminal image for Surface Pro 11 — v23

Experimental community image rebuilt with Lexr `v0.4.0-rc.2-24-g4c8aaf5` from the authenticated AArch64 rootfs snapshot. This is a terminal live USB with a guided installation option; no desktop is installed in the live image or preselected for installation. It is not an official Arch Linux or Arch Linux ARM installer release.

**Start here: [Arch Linux ARM installation quickstart](https://github.com/ooaklee/lexr.sh/blob/4c8aaf5bda4c813938275633d08fed93260ede45/docs/user-guide/arch-linux-arm-quickstart.md).** This link is pinned to the image's producer revision and works both while [Lexr PR #55](https://github.com/ooaklee/lexr.sh/pull/55) is under review and after it merges. Once merged, the [quickstart on main](https://github.com/ooaklee/lexr.sh/blob/main/docs/user-guide/arch-linux-arm-quickstart.md) will track subsequent changes.

## What is included

- Kernel `7.2.0-jg-0sp11v23-qcom-x1e`, matching modules and explicit X1E/OLED and X1P/LCD device trees, with ARM64 GRUB. Installed-system support targets X1E/OLED.
- A terminal live session, NetworkManager, public Wi-Fi board data and `lexr-arch-setup` for networking, the guide and installation. The temporary local account is `arch` with passwordless sudo.
- Bundled Archinstall 4.4 with Lexr's Surface integration: native kernel packaging, matching installed initramfs/DTB, ARM64 GRUB, ARM package checks and Adreno graphics choices. Archinstall handles the disk layout, account and optional desktop selections. This integration does not make every upstream Archinstall option supported on ARM64.
- Current Linux ARM64 Lexr, matching source, catalogues and legal notices, retained after installation. Optional `lexr kernel boot register-arch` can add the installed Arch loader to another OS's existing GRUB menu after a reviewed dry run.
- Updated `LEXR_GETTING_STARTED.txt` for Wi-Fi, pen/IPTSD, audio and microphone setup, power profiles, native Arch camera packages, and first-login troubleshooting. After installation, read it with `cat /usr/share/lexr/LEXR_GETTING_STARTED.txt`.

Pen and FullIO userspaces are downloaded explicitly using the guide's Lexr commands; they are not separately bundled or automatically installed in this ISO. Audio also requires permitted same-device private firmware and the documented installed-system setup. The camera preview uses native Arch packages. No private firmware, credentials, SSH keys, ngrok configuration or personal capture files are included. Do not restart the audio DSP while it supplies storage for a running live USB.

## Validation and hardware status

**This rebuilt ISO has passed Lexr creation and independent structural validation (6 checks), plus split-release preparation and validation. It has not yet been booted or installed on physical hardware.** Updating the embedded Lexr and initramfs setup creates new image bytes; earlier tests do not qualify this exact ISO.

Ooaklee previously tested candidate4, built with Lexr `2e0d384`, on Surface Pro 11 X1E/OLED: terminal live boot and Wi-Fi, guided installation to an internal ext4 partition, installed v23 kernel boot, touchscreen and Wi-Fi connectivity. Later installed-system setup confirmed pen input, clean stereo speakers, microphone input, power-profile switching, and a front-camera picture with its privacy light on. Those later checks used separately applied userspace/firmware changes; they do not mean all these features work automatically from a fresh installation.

The [hardware test record](https://github.com/ooaklee/lexr.sh/blob/4c8aaf5bda4c813938275633d08fed93260ede45/docs/operator-manual/arch-linux-arm-install.md#hardware-test-record) identifies the earlier ISO and the remaining work. X1P/LCD and other Snapdragon devices, cross-ABI upgrades, recovery and repeated multiboot selection remain unqualified. Camera tuning/lifecycle and hardware graphics acceleration need further testing. Disable Secure Boot for the unsigned kernel and external DTB.

## Download, verify and write with Lexr

Use Linux or macOS with `curl`, GitHub CLI (`gh`), `zstd`, `shasum`, Git and Go 1.26 or newer. Image validation and writing require Docker with a running daemon and Linux ARM64 container support. Allow at least 24 GiB of free workspace plus room for the downloaded parts and reconstructed ISO.

Run these commands in Bash as your regular user. The installer downloads the latest published Lexr, verifies its checksum and installs it on your PATH:

```bash
set -euo pipefail
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ooaklee/lexr.sh/refs/heads/main/install.sh | sh
export PATH="${LEXR_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}:$PATH"
LEXR="$(command -v lexr)"
"$LEXR" version

WORK="$(mktemp -d "$HOME/lexr-arch.XXXXXX")"
cd "$WORK"
```

**At publication, released Lexr versions predate this Arch image/release integration. Run the following pinned-source build too.** Once a stable release containing PR #55 and its Arch release support is available, the installer above is sufficient and this source-build fallback can be skipped. Until then, all commands below must use the pinned binary through `$LEXR`.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ooaklee/lexr.sh.git lexr-source
git -C lexr-source checkout --detach 4c8aaf5bda4c813938275633d08fed93260ede45
(cd lexr-source && go run ./cmd/lexr-build)
LEXR="$PWD/lexr-source/bin/lexr"
"$LEXR" version
```

Download the complete asset set and verify it before reconstructing the ISO:

```bash
TAG=sp11-arch-linux-arm-terminal-v23-20260909
gh release download "$TAG" --repo ooaklee/linux-surface-pro-11-oe --dir image-assets
(cd image-assets && shasum -a256 -c SHA256SUMS)
"$LEXR" image release validate image-assets

ISO=sp11-arch-linux-arm-terminal-v23-20260909.iso
cat "image-assets/$ISO".zst.part-* | zstd --decompress --stdout > "$ISO"
printf '%s  %s\n' 'b4284b022ebe1ef662a01ba382add81f470186cf49dc9bf1031cc6d4ac15b8c8' "$ISO" | shasum -a256 -c -
"$LEXR" image validate "$ISO"
"$LEXR" image devices
```

Keep the reconstructed ISO outside `image-assets`; that directory must contain exactly the published release members. Stop if a checksum or validation fails.

Choose the **whole USB device** by its identity and size. Writing erases that USB. Replace the placeholder after reviewing `image devices`, then preview and perform the write in an interactive terminal:

```bash
DEVICE="<reviewed-whole-USB-device>"
"$LEXR" image write "$ISO" --device "$DEVICE" --dry-run
sudo "$LEXR" image write "$ISO" --device "$DEVICE"
```

Lexr requests device/image confirmation, writes the ISO, verifies its complete length by reading it back and ejects the USB. Wait for its successful receipt before reconnecting and booting **X1E/OLED**.

## Boot and install

In the live terminal:

```bash
lexr-arch-setup
sudo nmtui
sudo archinstall
```

Use the [quickstart's partition guidance](https://github.com/ooaklee/lexr.sh/blob/4c8aaf5bda4c813938275633d08fed93260ede45/docs/user-guide/arch-linux-arm-quickstart.md#2-select-only-the-space-reserved-for-arch). Select manual partitioning, use a new/reserved ext4 root, and reuse an existing EFI System Partition at `/boot/efi` without formatting it, or create an ESP if none exists. Keep other partitions unassigned and keep Arch's `/boot` inside its own root. Encryption, LVM and separate Arch `/boot` are outside this supported flow. Review exactly what will be formatted; Archinstall executes your selected layout. Keep the Surface kernel and GRUB, then choose your account and optional environment. Start the bundled installer before upgrading live-session packages, because the integration targets its pinned Archinstall version.

Follow the quickstart through one-time first boot, optional persistent registration in an existing GRUB menu, and the installed-system setup guide. Installing a newer host Lexr does not update the Lexr already embedded in this fixed ISO.

## Image identity and source

- ISO: `sp11-arch-linux-arm-terminal-v23-20260909.iso`, **2,221,146,112 bytes**.
- ISO SHA-256: `b4284b022ebe1ef662a01ba382add81f470186cf49dc9bf1031cc6d4ac15b8c8`.
- Producer and embedded Lexr: [4c8aaf5bda4c813938275633d08fed93260ede45](https://github.com/ooaklee/lexr.sh/commit/4c8aaf5bda4c813938275633d08fed93260ede45), `v0.4.0-rc.2-24-g4c8aaf5`.
- Input: `arch-linux-arm-aarch64-20260805`, authenticated Arch Linux ARM AArch64 rootfs, **829,367,415 bytes**, SHA-256 `42a4eeaa038994ffd31fa173256ef2f0ef511358eeb41b9ea1f8626391b9b319`. The upstream `latest` URL is mutable; this release uses retained snapshot bytes. [Source intake and signature evidence](https://github.com/ooaklee/lexr.sh/blob/4c8aaf5bda4c813938275633d08fed93260ede45/docs/operator-manual/arch-linux-arm-source.md).
- Additional terminal/live packages use [the producer's fixed archive and signature lock](https://github.com/ooaklee/lexr.sh/blob/4c8aaf5bda4c813938275633d08fed93260ede45/internal/image/archlinux/packages.lock.json); installation can still download current ARM packages from the distribution's rolling repositories.
- Kernel packages, corresponding source and terms: [SP11 v23 kernel release](https://github.com/ooaklee/linux-surface-pro-11-oe/releases/tag/sp11-qcom-x1e-7.2.0-jg-0sp11v23). Lexr source and legal notices are also retained inside the companion.
- OE tag anchor: `aba8c0b65ea73422c8e15868606bb934780a066e`, the existing v23 support-source commit; the separate Lexr revision above identifies this image's implementation.

The closed assets were generated using `lexr image release prepare` and verified using `lexr image release validate`. They contain split zstd parts, the image manifest, `image-release-manifest.json`, generated `RELEASE-NOTES.md` and `SHA256SUMS`. The original private creation journal is not published. All six assets were downloaded afresh from OE and passed their checksum and closed-release checks. Reconstructing those uploaded parts produced the exact ISO hash and size above, and all six independent image checks passed using the documented pinned-source Lexr build.

Implementation and review: [Lexr PR #55](https://github.com/ooaklee/lexr.sh/pull/55). Qualification and reports: [Lexr issue #52](https://github.com/ooaklee/lexr.sh/issues/52). Related images: [Ubuntu Concept 26.04 v23](https://github.com/ooaklee/linux-surface-pro-11-oe/releases/tag/sp11-ubuntu-concept-26.04-v23-20260905), [elementary OS 8.1 v23](https://github.com/ooaklee/linux-surface-pro-11-oe/releases/tag/sp11-elementary-os-8.1-v23-20260906). Include the exact ISO hash, kernel, device variant and tested features when reporting results.
